b. ἀρεσσάμενος: having propitiated, having treated kindly. LgP
851. ἀνέσχε: the drug was brought up. LgP
854-59a. τῆς οἵην τ’ ἐν ὄρε〈σ〉σι: he called the liquid sap that is carried off from the oak.

b. Κασπίῃ ἐν κόχλῳ: the Caspian sea in the ocean, near which is also the Caspian nation, bordering on the Persians. The ocean has very large shells; on which, he says, 〈...〉 the Promethean drug. The poet in particular tells marvels about the root; for in none of the root-cutters
18 παρὰ τῷ ὠκ. in F, πλησίον ὠκεανοῦ from sch. c in P, but it is clear that the interpreter considered the Caspian Sea as a gulf of the ocean

has it been mentioned. He says its flower is similar to Corycian saffron; Corycium is a region of Cilicia, in which excellent saffron grows.

2 Et. Gen. (AB) Κωρύκιον: after the words cited at sch. II 705/11 b: here Corycium is a place (B, city A) of Cilicia (sch., Lyc- A B), in which excellent saffron grows. Such as III 853-857. Because, he says, the earth produced a plant from the ichor of Prometheus' liver, which the eagle let fall while eating his liver on the Caucasus mountain. Diosc. Mat. med. I 26 Strab. XIV 670 Plin. Nat. hist. XXI 31

c. About the Caspian Sea Artemidorus gives an account in his Epitome of the Geographies (fg 18 Stiehle Phil. 11, 1856, 242). It is near the ocean, where lies a nation named Caspian, bordering on the Persians.
11 sch. Lyc. 698. 1176 Clem. Al. Protr. II 15, 1 with sch. Et. M. 213, 49
860. ἑπτὰ μὲν ἀενάοις: having bathed in the waters of seven ever-flowing rivers. He tells marvels.

861. ἑπτάκι δὲ Βριμώ: seven times, he says, she called upon Hecate; for sorceresses are thought to invoke Hecate. He called her Brimo because of the fearful and terrifying nature of the goddess and because she sends apparitions called Hecataea and often changes her own form, for which reason she is also called Empusa. Or from the roar of fire — 'for such is the roar' (Ξ 396) —, for the goddess is torch-bearing. The element βρι indicates intensity, as in 'βριήπυος ὄβριμος Ἄρης' (Ν 521); perhaps then Brimo is she who has great wrath, being a kind of βρίμηνις.

864-66. Τιτηνίδος: since Prometheus was one of the Titans. Therefore he called the root Titanid, because it sprouted from Prometheus, who was one of the Titans. For this reason he tells marvels about the cutting of the root and Prometheus' suffering at its cutting.
